answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to hold the cipher of valid state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random memory indices; failure to return data matching the ember of the working set triggers a penalty. This mirror of latency ensures each agent keeps unique bus access. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain status, while 1,000 fakes incur 120,000 watts, rendering mass-identity farms infeasible.
